_comment: Corrections to the primary paper we attribute to a dandiset.
The pipeline derives primary papers from a dandiset's relatedResource
entries and, failing that, from DOIs mentioned in its description. Both
sources can be wrong in ways that matter, because every citation to a
dandiset's primary paper is treated as a candidate reuse of that dandiset.
A wrong primary paper therefore pulls in every paper citing an unrelated
Each entry gives the reason, so these can be re-examined when DANDI's own
metadata changes and the override becomes unnecessary.
replace: use these DOIs instead of whatever was derived
remove:  drop these DOIs from whatever was derived

reason: No primary paper reached the corpus. DANDI links the paper in
relatedResource, but by a URL without a DOI or with a non-paper resource
type, so the pipeline skipped it: "VIP interneurons in mouse primary
visual cortex selectively enhance responses to weak but specific
stimuli" (2020). Contributors who are also authors: Millman, Dan, Vries,

This dandiset registers no relatedResource at all, so the DOI was scraped
from its description, where it appears as background: the description
cites Andermann et al. 2011 to explain why speed tuning is interesting.
It is a citation to prior work, not a paper describing this data.
Inheriting its citations attributed 47 papers to this dandiset, 42 of
which named the Allen Institute.
No replacement is given because this dataset appears to have no describing
publication. It is a standalone Allen Institute deposit contributed by
Millman and de Vries. With no primary paper, the indirect pathway simply
will not cover it, which is correct: there is nothing to cite.

DANDI registers this as IsSupplementTo 10.1038/s41586-020-03171-x, the
Siegle et al. 2021 Visual Coding survey. That paper describes the Allen
Brain Observatory platform, not the Global/Local Oddball experiment held
in this dandiset, and it is very widely cited. Attributing its citations
to 000253 pulled in 54 papers of which 48 named the Allen Institute and
none mentioned OpenScope or the oddball paradigm at all; their own quotes
describe using Visual Coding data through the AllenSDK.
The replacement is the paper that points at this dandiset rather than the
other way round: its data availability statement reads 'All mouse data
used in this work are openly available through the DANDI Archive
(dandiset id: 000253)'. It has appeared under several titles and is also
indexed as PMC11741236; revisit if it acquires a journal DOI.
